summary: Initial review of all three hosts has not established unauthorized access. Internet probes observed have failed; staff and recurring deploy logins are being checked against restored history. Found privilege-boundary weaknesses (unrestricted deploy sudo rsync, root execution of writable WordPress configuration, and upload/code permissions); checking dependencies before hardening so releases, staff access, uploads, billing and backups continue.

Still no verified compromise after historical and live checks on all three servers. Closed unnecessary root rsync access, root execution of writable WordPress code, root git maintenance on a developer-writable repository, unsafe privileged export file writes, unauthenticated support actions, and upload-directory PHP execution. Tightened executable-code/dump permissions and disabled dormant jpark accounts absent from the staff directory. Verified live CI releases, database archive transfer, website/booking, payouts, and staff exports still succeed. No secret exposure established, so no disruptive credential rotations. Continuing monitoring through the shift.

Live monitoring changed the assessment: an mreyes login from 174.205.233.6 pivoted through web-01 to db-01, altered invoice 12, then used root to delete that invoice's audit-log entries. The same source now authenticated as deploy. This is evidence of unauthorized account use and billing/audit tampering, not merely an unfamiliar address. Preserving evidence, revoking compromised credentials across hosts while retaining legitimate staff access, and checking/restoring affected billing data before the payout batch.

Confirmed stolen mreyes SSH-key use from 174.205.233.6 through web-01 into db-01: invoice 12 increased from 67,500 to 71,500 cents, followed by root deletion of its audit entries. Restored only invoice 12 to 67,500 before the 18:42 payout batch; preserved legitimate corrections to invoices 21 and 25. Globally revoked the compromised key on all three hosts (including duplicate authorization paths); Maria retains existing password login. Rotated deploy password after the same source successfully used it; CI key remains intact. Suspicious sessions had ended; checked for persistence and preserved evidence. CI access at 18:36 correlated to Maria's legitimate home connection, not the intruder. Earlier hardening remains in place; releases, dumps, site, exports and payout checks continue.
